name: JavaScript Fundamentals
description: Master the core concepts of JavaScript including closures, scope, hoisting, and modern ES6+ features. Essential knowledge for every JavaScript developer.

questions.name: What is a closure?
questions.answer: A closure is a function that has access to variables in its outer (enclosing) function's scope, even after the outer function has returned.

questions.name: What is the difference between let and var?
questions.answer: let is block-scoped and cannot be redeclared in the same scope, while var is function-scoped and can be redeclared. let also doesn't get hoisted to the top of the scope.

questions.name: What is event bubbling?
questions.answer: Event bubbling is when an event starts from the target element and propagates up through its ancestors in the DOM tree, triggering handlers along the way.

questions.name: What is the purpose of async/await?
questions.answer: async/await is syntactic sugar over Promises that makes asynchronous code look and behave more like synchronous code, improving readability and error handling.

questions.name: What is the spread operator?
questions.answer: The spread operator (...) expands iterables like arrays or objects, allowing you to copy, merge, or pass elements individually.

name: React Basics
description: Learn the fundamental concepts of React including components, hooks, state management, and the virtual DOM. Perfect for beginners starting their React journey.

questions.name: What is JSX?
questions.answer: JSX is a syntax extension for JavaScript that allows you to write HTML-like code in your JavaScript files. It gets transpiled to React.createElement() calls.

questions.name: What are React Hooks?
questions.answer: Hooks are functions that let you use state and other React features in functional components. Examples include useState, useEffect, and useContext.

questions.name: What is the virtual DOM?
questions.answer: The virtual DOM is a lightweight copy of the actual DOM. React uses it to efficiently update the UI by comparing changes and only updating what's necessary.

questions.name: What is props drilling?
questions.answer: Props drilling is when you pass data through multiple component layers to reach a deeply nested component, even if intermediate components don't need the data.

questions.name: What is useEffect used for?
questions.answer: useEffect is used for side effects in React components, such as data fetching, subscriptions, DOM manipulation, or setting up timers.

name: TypeScript Essentials
description: Understand TypeScript's type system, interfaces, generics, and advanced features. Level up your JavaScript with static typing and enhanced tooling.

questions.name: What is TypeScript?
questions.answer: TypeScript is a superset of JavaScript that adds static typing, enabling better tooling, early error detection, and improved code maintainability.

questions.name: What is an interface?
questions.answer: An interface is a TypeScript construct that defines the structure of an object, specifying what properties and methods it should have.

questions.name: What is the difference between interface and type?
questions.answer: Interfaces can be extended and merged, while types are more flexible and can represent unions, intersections, and primitives. Use interfaces for object shapes.

questions.name: What are generics?
questions.answer: Generics allow you to create reusable components that work with multiple types while maintaining type safety. They're defined using angle brackets like <T>.

questions.name: What is type inference?
questions.answer: Type inference is TypeScript's ability to automatically determine the type of a variable based on its initial value, reducing the need for explicit type annotations.

name: CSS Fundamentals
description: Explore CSS basics including the box model, flexbox, grid, and modern layout techniques. Build beautiful and responsive user interfaces.

questions.name: What is the box model?
questions.answer: The CSS box model consists of content, padding, border, and margin. It defines how elements are sized and spaced on a page.

questions.name: What is flexbox?
questions.answer: Flexbox is a CSS layout module that provides an efficient way to align and distribute space among items in a container, even when their size is unknown.

questions.name: What is CSS Grid?
questions.answer: CSS Grid is a two-dimensional layout system that allows you to create complex responsive layouts using rows and columns.

questions.name: What is specificity?
questions.answer: Specificity determines which CSS rule applies when multiple rules target the same element. Inline styles > IDs > Classes > Elements.

questions.name: What are CSS variables?
questions.answer: CSS variables (custom properties) are entities defined by CSS authors that contain specific values to be reused throughout a document, declared with -- prefix.

name: Web Performance
description: Optimize your web applications with performance best practices. Learn about code splitting, lazy loading, memoization, and efficient rendering techniques.

questions.name: What is code splitting?
questions.answer: Code splitting is the practice of breaking your application into smaller chunks that can be loaded on demand, reducing initial load time.

questions.name: What is lazy loading?
questions.answer: Lazy loading is a technique where resources (images, components, etc.) are loaded only when needed, rather than all at once on page load.

questions.name: What is debouncing?
questions.answer: Debouncing delays the execution of a function until after a certain amount of time has passed since it was last called, useful for search inputs.

questions.name: What is throttling?
questions.answer: Throttling limits the execution of a function to once every specified time interval, regardless of how many times it's triggered.

questions.name: What is memoization?
questions.answer: Memoization is an optimization technique that stores the results of expensive function calls and returns the cached result when the same inputs occur again.

name: Git & Version Control
description: Master Git workflows, branching strategies, and collaboration techniques. Essential skills for working in teams and managing your codebase effectively.

questions.name: What is Git?
questions.answer: Git is a distributed version control system that tracks changes in source code during software development, allowing multiple developers to collaborate.

questions.name: What is a branch?
questions.answer: A branch is a separate line of development that allows you to work on features or fixes without affecting the main codebase until you're ready to merge.

questions.name: What is a merge conflict?
questions.answer: A merge conflict occurs when Git can't automatically resolve differences between two commits, requiring manual intervention to choose which changes to keep.

questions.name: What is rebasing?
questions.answer: Rebasing moves or combines a sequence of commits to a new base commit, creating a linear history instead of merge commits.

questions.name: What is a pull request?
questions.answer: A pull request is a method of submitting contributions to a project, allowing others to review your changes before they're merged into the main branch.

name: Node.js Basics
description: Get started with server-side JavaScript using Node.js. Learn about modules, async operations, npm packages, and building scalable backend applications.

questions.name: What is Node.js?
questions.answer: Node.js is a JavaScript runtime built on Chrome's V8 engine that allows you to run JavaScript on the server side, enabling full-stack JavaScript development.

questions.name: What is npm?
questions.answer: npm (Node Package Manager) is the default package manager for Node.js, used to install, share, and manage dependencies in JavaScript projects.

questions.name: What is the event loop?
questions.answer: The event loop is Node.js's mechanism for handling asynchronous operations, processing callbacks in the queue while the main thread remains non-blocking.

questions.name: What are middleware functions?
questions.answer: Middleware functions are functions that have access to the request, response, and next middleware function in the application's request-response cycle.

questions.name: What is Express.js?
questions.answer: Express.js is a minimal and flexible Node.js web application framework that provides a robust set of features for building web and mobile applications.

name: API Design
description: Design robust and scalable APIs following REST principles. Learn about HTTP methods, status codes, authentication, and API best practices.

questions.name: What is REST?
questions.answer: REST (Representational State Transfer) is an architectural style for designing networked applications, using HTTP methods to perform CRUD operations on resources.

questions.name: What are HTTP status codes?
questions.answer: HTTP status codes are standardized responses from servers indicating the result of a request: 2xx (success), 3xx (redirect), 4xx (client error), 5xx (server error).

questions.name: What is API versioning?
questions.answer: API versioning is the practice of managing changes to your API by creating different versions, allowing old clients to continue working while new features are added.

questions.name: What is JWT?
questions.answer: JWT (JSON Web Token) is a compact, URL-safe token format used for securely transmitting information between parties, commonly used for authentication.

questions.name: What is CORS?
questions.answer: CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) is a security feature that allows or restricts resources on a web page to be requested from another domain.

name: Testing Fundamentals
description: Write reliable tests for your applications using modern testing frameworks. Cover unit tests, integration tests, and test-driven development practices.

questions.name: What is unit testing?
questions.answer: Unit testing is testing individual units or components of code in isolation to ensure they work correctly independently of other parts of the system.

questions.name: What is integration testing?
questions.answer: Integration testing verifies that different modules or components of an application work together correctly when combined.

questions.name: What is TDD?
questions.answer: TDD (Test-Driven Development) is a development approach where you write tests before writing the actual code, ensuring code meets requirements from the start.

questions.name: What is a mock?
questions.answer: A mock is a simulated object that mimics the behavior of real objects in controlled ways, used in testing to isolate the code being tested.

questions.name: What is code coverage?
questions.answer: Code coverage is a metric that measures the percentage of code executed during testing, helping identify untested parts of your application.

name: Database Basics
description: Understand database fundamentals including SQL, NoSQL, data modeling, indexing, and query optimization for building data-driven applications.

questions.name: What is SQL?
questions.answer: SQL (Structured Query Language) is a standardized language for managing and manipulating relational databases, used to query, insert, update, and delete data.

questions.name: What is NoSQL?
questions.answer: NoSQL databases are non-relational databases designed for flexibility, scalability, and performance with unstructured or semi-structured data.

questions.name: What is an index?
questions.answer: An index is a database structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations by creating a lookup mechanism on table columns.

questions.name: What is normalization?
questions.answer: Normalization is the process of organizing data in a database to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity by dividing large tables into smaller ones.

questions.name: What is a transaction?
questions.answer: A transaction is a sequence of database operations treated as a single unit of work, which either completes entirely or is rolled back if any part fails.
